summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause with limited incidents: the US has carried out what it calls limited strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran reports new mine strikes on tankers, and President Trump says the US blockade of Iran's land supply routes is now in effect while Qatar-mediated talks go on; President Trump says new attacks are unlikely if talks progress. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are controlled by the US and its regional partners. Most traffic moves through a shuttle system the US coordinates with Arab partners, with weekly volumes swinging as attacks continue (Al Jazeera).

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: About 11.6 million barrels a day over the seven days to Oct 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline (Kpler, via Al Jazeera).

status.label: The war
status.note: US officials said the US carried out limited, defensive strikes on Iranian targets, including on Qeshm Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Nov 2, after Iranian surface-to-air missile threats; they said it was not a resumption of major combat (Wall Street Journal, then Reuters). Indirect talks through Qatari mediators continue with no breakthrough announced; Vice President Vance said there has been progress. On Nov 7 the US carried out further strikes on Iranian air defences on Qeshm Island, which President Trump called minor (Euronews). On Nov 8 Trump told CNN renewed attacks were highly unlikely if talks make real progress; no deal has been signed.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent settled Friday, Nov 6, at about US$98.32 a barrel and WTI at about US$90.83, both down about 13% on the week, which Rigzone (Bloomberg) called the biggest weekly drop since 2022 (some outlets say since 2020), on hopes that the US election result brings an Iran deal; Thursday Brent had settled at US$98.29 after more tanker attacks (EnergyNow; Rigzone; Nation Thailand).

updates.text: After meeting Qatar's prime minister, President Trump said the war with Iran is militarily effectively over and that renewed US strikes are quite unlikely, and that Gulf allies back the Iron Gate blockade; Secretary of State Rubio called Iran's conditions for reopening Hormuz outrageous. No deal has been announced.
President Trump said the new US blockade of Iran's land supply routes, run by a task force called Iron Gate, is in effect; Iran has played the task force down. No deal has been announced.
Iran said no unauthorised vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz overnight after navigation aids in the strait were destroyed.

President Trump told CNN that renewed attacks on Iran are highly unlikely if talks make real progress on the nuclear programme and reopening Hormuz, but that it depends on Iran signing a very strong agreement; oil prices dipped on the remarks. Iran says it will not discuss nuclear issues until the blockade ends.

A Saudi-led coalition spokesman said air defences intercepted missiles and a drone aimed at Riyadh (outlets report different counts); the energy ministry said shrapnel caused minor damage to an Aramco administrative building, with no injuries.
UKMTO reported a tanker fire about 8 nautical miles northwest of Khasab, Oman, at about 19:20 UTC on Saturday, Nov 7; the crew was evacuated and no casualties were reported.

The Houthis claimed responsibility on Sunday for an attack on Saudi Aramco that damaged a building through falling shrapnel; they also said Saudi strikes killed dozens in Yemen's Sanaa province, which Fox News said it could not confirm.

The IRGC navy said three ships were burning early Sunday after using what it called unauthorised routes through the strait, and says at least 12 ships have caught fire this month, mostly after hitting mines; UKMTO said most such incidents could not be independently verified.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
